one_liner: Research StarPU task-based sparse Cholesky/LDL^T solver built on SPRAL SSIDS kernels; no published speedup in the repo.
what_it_does: Solves large sparse symmetric systems by direct factorization: Cholesky for positive-definite matrices, and LDL^T with 1x1/2x2 pivots for indefinite ones (a disabled, undocumented unsymmetric-pattern LU path also exists). The API is SPRAL/HSL style in Fortran 2003 (sylver_init, then spldlt_analyse, spldlt_factor, spldlt_solve, spldlt_free, then sylver_finalize), with a partial C interface under src/interfaces/C. It reuses SPRAL's analysis and CPU kernels, so it behaves like a different scheduler for SSIDS rather than a drop-in for PARDISO or MA87.
how_it_is_fast: The multifrontal factorization is written as a sequential task flow: fronts are split into blocks (block size nb), and each block operation is submitted as a task to StarPU, which builds the DAG and schedules it across CPU cores and, optionally, NVIDIA GPUs (lws or heteroprio schedulers). Indefinite factorization uses A Posteriori Threshold Pivoting (APTP), which factors blocks optimistically and checks stability afterwards, so pivoting does not serialise the column sweep; failed pivots are delayed or redone with TPP. This is the method of Duff-Hogg-Lopez (NLAFET Working Note 21 / SSIDS v2), which per search snippets performs favourably against HSL MA86, HSL MA97 and PARDISO on multicore, but those numbers are for SSIDS, not for this repo.
when_to_use: Research on runtime-system (StarPU) scheduling of sparse direct solvers, as a worked example of an STF multifrontal Cholesky/LDL^T on CPU+GPU nodes.
Studying or reproducing NLAFET-era APTP and heterogeneous-scheduling results where you need the StarPU variant of SSIDS rather than the OpenMP one.
Large symmetric indefinite systems on one multicore node with optional NVIDIA GPUs, when you already run StarPU and SPRAL and can tolerate prototype code.
when_not_to_use: Production solves: the last commit was 2020-05-11, there are no releases, CI was Travis, and no benchmarks or regression results are published; use SPRAL SSIDS, MUMPS, PARDISO or CHOLMOD instead.
When you need the factors: open issue #2 (March 2020, unanswered) reports that L and D cannot be obtained from spldlt_factorize().
Unsymmetric systems: the splu path is commented out of the documentation and has no driver beyond splu_test.F90.
Simple builds: it needs StarPU >= 1.3, a SPRAL submodule pinned to commit f71ab9e (branch 'gpufix'), MeTiS, hwloc, a sequential BLAS/LAPACK, and Fortran, C and C++ compilers, plus CUDA for GPU runs.
Distributed-memory (MPI) runs: nothing in the README or CMake options offers them.

integration.dependencies: StarPU >= 1.3 (or sequential STF runtime), SPRAL (git submodule, built automatically), MeTiS, hwloc, sequential BLAS/LAPACK (MKL/ESSL/OpenBLAS); optional CUDA, CUTLASS, OpenMP
integration.min_toolchain: C++11 (CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 11), Fortran 2003 compiler, CMake; CUDA toolkit for GPU builds
integration.platforms: Linux x86-64 and IBM POWER (ESSL recommended there) are implied by the README; NVIDIA GPUs optional; other platforms not documented
integration.thread_safety: not documented (parallelism is internal via StarPU; global sylver_init/sylver_finalize suggests one solver context per process)
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — API mirrors SPRAL SSIDS's analyse/factor/solve cycle in Fortran, but uses its own spldlt_* names and init/finalize; not a drop-in for PARDISO, MA87 or CHOLMOD

gotchas: It must be linked against a sequential BLAS/LAPACK (README); a threaded BLAS oversubscribes cores under StarPU.

It includes SPRAL's internal C++ headers (ssids/cpu/cpu_iface.hxx, ThreadStats.hxx), so it is coupled to the pinned SPRAL submodule commit; building against a current SPRAL release is not documented and may break.
STARPU_DIR must be set in the environment for FindSTARPU.cmake, and the default runtime is StarPU, so a plain cmake without StarPU fails unless you pass -D SYLVER_RUNTIME=STF.
The docs claim bit-compatible results, but no test evidence for that is in the repo.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Choose SPRAL SSIDS, which carries the same APTP kernels in a maintained OpenMP/CUDA library with published comparisons, for real solves; pick SyLVER only to study or extend the StarPU task-based variant. For SPD-only problems with published speedups over CHOLMOD, BaSpaCho or Sympiler are better documented.
verified_claims_summary: The repo has no measured result: the README and doc pages only say the DAG algorithms 'enable an efficient exploitation of multicore CPU architectures and GPU-accelerated systems'. The related NLAFET papers (SpLLT vs HSL MA87 on 28 cores, reported only as 'comparable performance'; SSIDS v2 APTP vs MA86/MA97/PARDISO, 'performs favourably') were seen as search snippets only, because nlafet.eu, researchgate and epubs.stfc.ac.uk are blocked here, and they measure sibling codes, not SyLVER.
status_note: Abandoned since May 2020 (EU H2020 NLAFET project ended), with 844 commits, 13 stars and one unanswered issue; BSD-3-Clause so copyable, but a research prototype with heavy dependencies.
sources_read: WebSearch snippets: aimsciences.org naco.2018014 abstract (SpLLT vs HSL MA87), NLAFET WN21 / RAL-TR-2016-017 abstract (SSIDS APTP vs MA86, MA97, PARDISO)
